title: Change-impact simulator and offline regression playbook for embedding + reranker quality
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: We frequently observe small config or model variant updates (quantization profiles, kv-cache parameters, batching windows, or newer open-model checkpoints) that produce subtle degradations in offline ranking or recall for search/relevance flows. Existing probes focus on scalar drift alerts but lack a stable, reproducible offline simulator that predicts end-to-end recall/precision impact across top-k thresholds and cohorts prior to rollout.

Scope: Build a change-impact simulator and a playbook that ties config/model change diffs to deterministic offline evals and drift statistics for embeddings + reranker pipelines. The simulator will be used by CI and by the rollout controller to gate canaries and automated rollbacks.

Goals:
- Produce stable offline metrics that correlate with production user-visible regressions (top-1/top-5 recall, nDCG@k, R-Precision).
- Surface distributional drift signals (embedding distance shifts, cosine similarity CDF shifts, KS/Wasserstein scores) and cohort-level delta summaries.
- Attach confidence bands and sample-size driven thresholds so small, noisy changes don't trigger false positives.
- Integrate with existing sentinel/alerting infra and provide a concise playbook for triage and automated remediation.

Design overview:
- Change diff ingestion: when a PR/modification is proposed (model, quantization file, runtime config), CI will bundle a deterministic snapshot of the change and trigger the simulator.
- Datasets: use the seeded offline eval corpus with stratified cohorts (query intent buckets, high-frequency vs long-tail, geo). We'll sample N=50k queries (strata-driven) for stable estimates.
- Metrics: top-1/top-5 recall@k, nDCG@5, reranker precision@k, pairwise concordance (Kendall tau), embedding shift metrics (mean cosine delta, 90p-10p span), and population-level KS/Wasserstein per-cohort.
- Statistical gating: compute bootstrapped confidence intervals and run a sign-test / paired t-test for paired scores. Define hysteresis windows (e.g., require 95% CI excluding baseline or sustained delta > threshold across 3 cycles).
- Synthetic perturbation mode: to estimate sensitivity, the simulator can inject controlled noise (L2 perturbations) to derive metric sensitivity curves and recommend minimal detectable effect sizes for the current sample.
- Output: a human-readable regression report plus machine-readable JSON summary consumed by rollout engine (keys: primary_metric, delta, p_value, risk_level, recommended_action).

Acceptance criteria:
- CI/PR integration triggers the simulator on model/config changes and returns a report within acceptable CI bounds (<20 minutes for the 50k sample run using cached embeddings).
- Simulator produces reproducible deltas with bootstrapped CIs and a recommended action code (accept/canary/reject).
- Dashboard: a new per-change view in Console showing baseline vs candidate metric curves, cohort deltas, and distribution plots with link to the sample that produced the report.
- Playbook: documented triage steps for high/medium/low risk signals, and an automated rollback hook that the rollout controller can call with a regression ticket.

Implementation plan:
- Phase 1 (2 sprints): implement the core simulator library (data sampling, metric computation, bootstrapping, drift stats). Expose a CLI + REST endpoint for CI.
- Phase 2 (1 sprint): integrate with PR pipeline (GitHub action), persist reports to internal S3 and index in the Console backend.
- Phase 3 (1 sprint): Console UI + rollout gating integration (canary automation). Add synthetic perturbation harness.

Runbook & Playbook (high level):
- Low risk: delta within CI and < pre-defined thresholds => auto-approve.
- Medium risk: delta crosses threshold on one cohort but not global => create a triage ticket, run targeted shadow eval (10k queries) and consider canary rollout to 5% traffic.
- High risk: global metric regression with p<0.01 and effect size > recommended threshold => block rollout and create an incident with suggested rollback PR and automatic revert option.

Observability & dashboards:
- Add per-change metric historical traces and aggregated sensitivity heatmaps.
- Alerts: map simulator risk_level to severity and attach links to sample sets, PR, and a reproducible notebook.

Testing & validation:
- Correlate offline simulator outputs with recent production incidents (retrospective runs for last 6 months) and report true positive/false positive rates.
- Validate sensitivity using synthetic perturbations and known-good model swaps.

Artifacts and links:
- Preliminary spec: https://redwood.atlassian.com/confluence/embed-change-impact-simulator (draft)
- Sample report schema: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quality-harness/blob/main/schemas/change_report.json
- Shadow eval dashboard prototype: https://dash.redwood.company/emb-eval/prototype

Notes: The simulator should be conservative by default to avoid blocking small benign updates. We will iterate thresholds after retrospective validation.
